SUMMARY:
Theowners ofthis8.45-acre area at the northeast corner of Prairie Avenue and Frontier Mall Drive
have petitioned the City to annex theland into the City in order to sell the proposed Lot 1 to an
extended-stay hotel developer.The remaining proposed lot would remain undeveloped forthe time
being.A concurrent preliminary plat andzone change application hasbeen submitted aswell.
Wyoming State Statutes require that prior to annexing territory to the City certain stepsmust be
followed, including the governing body conducting a public hearing andfinding that the territory
is eligible for annexation.The statutes list six criteria thatmust be met for the territory to be eligible
for annexation.The attached resolution finds compliance with these six criteria.The attached
ordinance would approve the annexation, allowing the annexation map to be recorded and the
property brought into the City.Staff recommends adoption of the resolution and ordinance.
DESCRIPTION OF SITE AND SURROUNDINGS:
The subject property is approximately 8.45 acres of vacant land northeast of and adjacent to
Frontier Mall Drive and Prairie Avenue. On the east side of the property is the platted but unbuilt
Cutoff Road.The land raises several feet from Prairie Avenue, then slopes back down to where
Rue Terre aligns.Frontier Mall Drive is fully constructed including the sidewalk.Prairie Avenue
is built, but thesidewalk will need to be constructed as the property develops.Rue Terre and Cutoff
Road are not constructed.Prairie is considered a minor arterial roadway.Frontier Mall Drive and
Rue Terre are considered collectors.
Looking northwest at subject property from south side of Prairie Avenue.

COMPREHENSIVE PLAN:
LAND-USE AND ZONING: The property is within the Urban Service Boundary.The Future
Land Use Plan map in Plan Cheyenne indicates Community Business for this property, which is
primarily appropriate for general retail and office uses. Hotels and motels are a permitted use in
the CB zone district, which is proposed for this property in the associated zone change application.
POLICIES AND PRINCIPLES: Principle 3.1 in Plan Cheyenne states:“Our community will
our new neighborhoods will be designed to accommodate traffic growth”and Policy 2.2.c states,
inpart: Neighborhoods should have connected streets and sidewalks tomake walking and
bicycling safe and convenient.”The preliminary plat proposes dedicating right-of-way to match
the existing right-of-way of Rue Terre(140feetinwidth); however construction of the road would
not extend beyond the plat boundaries, meaning there will be no access to theproposed hotel from
Rue Terre until that section is constructed.Instead, motorists on Rue Terre or the Sam's Clubeast
of Rue Terre will have toget on Dell Range and turn onto Prairie Avenue to get to the hotel.Many
motorists cut through K-Mart's parking lot or drive behind the store. As discussed in the staff
Terre in this“missing link."
TRANSPORTATION: Similarly, the basic vision of the Transportation Plan is to provide residents
"an adequate, connected, multi-modal transportation system." The proposal completes a portion
of the missing section of Rue Terre but leaves approximately 460 feet un constructed.
ANNEXATION ELIGIBILITY DATA/ANALYSIS:
Before any territory is eligible for annexation, the governing body must find that the following
criteria are met (W.S.15-1-402 (a)):
1)“An annexation of the area is for the protection of the health, safety and welfare of the
persons residing in the area and in the city or town."Findings: Ensuring development
connects to City sewerrather than utilizing septic systems promotes public health for area
residents.Likewise, having development served by City police serves the public safety and
welfare of area residents.
2)“The urban development of the area sought to be annexed would constitute a natural,
geographical, economical and social part of the annexing city or town.”Findings: The
property abuts existing City limits on three sides and is part of a larger area surrounded by
annexed property.The site is located within the Plan Cheyenne comprehensive plan area
and planned for urban services expansion. People who will work in this area will likely
reside, shop, and recreate in Cheyenne facilities.
3）“The area sought to be annexed is a logical and feasible addition to the annexing city or
town and the extension ofbasic and other services customarily available to the residents of
the city or town shall, within reason, be available to the area proposed to be annexed.
Findings: The area sought to be annexed is planned for urban services expansion in
numerous City planning documents including Plan Cheyenne and the Board of Public
Utilities master plan.The City's water and sewer system has capacity to serve this area and
lines are in place on two sides of the property. Development will be required to include
extension of water and sewer lines, stormwater lines, and street improvements.Services
customarily available to residents in Cheyenne will be available to the subject property.
